cover letter

The University of California, Office of the President, is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This range takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, skills, knowledge, abilities, education, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position. Salary offers are determined based on final candidate qualifications and experience. The full salary range shows the growth potential for this position and the pay scale is the budgeted salary or hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position.
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training
Masters Degree and/or Juris Doctorate Degree from an ABA Accredited law school.
Minimum 8 years related experience or equivalent combination of education and experience.

The Labor Relations Manager is a high-level labor relations professional working closely with their assigned Associate Director of Labor Relations / Chief Negotiator (CN) on a portfolio of collective bargaining agreements. The Labor Relations Manager leads defined responsibilities in their designated workstream, including preparing and taking ownership over grievance responses, researching and evaluating bargaining proposals, working on contract implementation and drafting relevant guidance, and coordinating contract-administration work across the UC system. The Labor Relations Manager investigates issues, analyzes agreements and applicable law, prepares written responses and recommendations, and coordinates with campus and medical-center labor relations staff, labor partners, UC Legal, and other University partners as assigned. The role requires sound judgment, discretion, strong project-management skills, and the ability to communicate complex labor relations issues clearly to varied audiences. The Associate Director/Chief Negotiator sets the Labor Relations Manager's day-to-day priorities and assignments while leading the University's strategy and negotiations for assigned collective bargaining agreements. This position is eligible for a remote work arrangement within the state of California. The selected candidate must reside within the state of California or be willing to relocate.

30% Labor-Management Relations – Carry out day-to-day assignments from the CN related to union communications, labor-management meetings, and information requests. Prepare meeting agendas, research relevant agreements and past practice, document outcomes, and coordinate follow-up. Lead assigned requests for information by clarifying the request, identifying and reviewing responsive records, analyzing applicable law and agreement requirements, coordinating review with the CN, UC Legal, and other stakeholders as needed, and preparing draft responses for direction or approval as appropriate. Review proposed policy, procedural, and work-related changes for potential notice and bargaining obligations under HEERA, applicable agreements, and University processes; provide analysis and draft notices or supporting materials as assigned. Track commitments and coordinate implementation of agreed-upon items, keeping the CN informed of progress and issues.

40% Grievance Response, Contract Negotiations and Administration – Lead assigned grievance-response work for the portfolio of assigned collective bargaining agreements. This includes drafting and submitting grievance responses, tracking grievances as they move across the system to ensure timely responses, and using excellent judgement to determine when grievances should go to arbitration hearings. The Labor Relations Manager may occasionally serve as the University’s grievance hearing officer at designated steps when assigned. Provide contract interpretations and practical guidance to departments, managers, and campus or medical-center labor relations staff consistent with direction from the CN. Support the CN’s bargaining strategy by researching and evaluating union proposals and workplace issues; preparing draft University proposals, contract language, decision memoranda, bargaining materials, data, and authority requests; maintaining proposal and issue tracking; and coordinating input from stakeholders. Participate in systemwide or local negotiations as assigned, including taking notes, managing information requests, and presenting information when directed. The CN leads assigned systemwide negotiations and determines bargaining strategy and positions; the Manager does not independently commit the University to bargaining positions or agreements.

20% Dispute Resolution and Systemwide Coordination – Support the CN in managing disputes, including arbitrations and unfair labor practice matters. Work with UC Legal and outside counsel as assigned to organize facts, analyze applicable law, prepare briefing materials, and develop options for resolution, including draft side agreements and settlements. Participate in arbitration, unfair labor practice, and other proceedings when assigned. Coordinate assigned committees, collaborative meetings, cross-location input, data collection, training, and communications on contract interpretation, administration, and compliance. Elevate significant legal, operational, financial, or reputational risks to the CN promptly.

10% Case management, organization, and research – Maintain accurate and organized files and tracking for assigned grievances, information requests, arbitrations, unfair labor practice matters, settlements, bargaining assignments, and related deadlines. Research labor relations laws, administrative decisions, arbitration awards, past practices, and employment trends to support the CN’s analysis and recommendations. Identify recurring issues and risks, share findings with the CN, and recommend guidance or process improvements that support timely and consistent labor relations work. Perform other duties as assigned.
25% Travel throughout California for bargaining with unions and periodic team meetings.
Labor Relations Representative 4
Benefits: For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University visit: Benefits of Belonging
Possesses advanced analytical skills to conduct analysis and develop recommendations, demonstrating organization and problem-solving skills.
Demonstrates skills necessary to bargain and represent the organization's interests effectively.
Demonstrates advanced knowledge of organizational policies and procedures; advanced knowledge of functional area and understands how work impacts other areas in Human Resources and the organization.
Has advanced knowledge of labor/employment law and the principles and techniques of labor negotiations.

Demonstrates strong communication skills both written and oral that will be reflected in contract negotiations, drafting contract language, responding to union information requests and union grievances, decision memoranda, briefing documents, and all other written materials.

Demonstrates strong quantitative skills and an ability to use Microsoft Office programs including, but not limited to, Word, Excel, PowerPoint. Ability to effectively and professionally use video-conferencing platforms and applications. Must be able to work independently, effectively manage time, effectively communicate, and produce superior work product in an in-person or remote work environment.
Demonstrates advanced knowledge of the principles of advocacy in order to represent the organization in complex and sensitive dispute forums.
Has working knowledge of applicable state and federal labor laws and administrative decisions regarding labor relations related matters.
Possesses specialized knowledge within labor relations field.
